title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, grilled without sauce, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken legs, drumsticks and thighs grilled without sauce are a popular source of protein. The skin left on the meat adds extra flavor and contains beneficial fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken legs and thighs contain more iron than breast meat.
Grilling creates a flavorful crust that locks juices inside the meat.
Chicken skin is rich in collagen, which is good for skin and joints.
Dark chicken meat (legs, thighs) has a richer taste compared to white meat.
Grilling can reduce excess fat if the skin is removed after cooking.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 25 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: Dark chicken meat supplies iron for oxygen transport and zinc for immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken legs are high in vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6), important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: The skin contains collagen, which may support healthy skin, hair and nails.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: This dish contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The skin raises the calorie count and saturated fat, so people with high cholesterol should limit its intake.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked chicken can harbor salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium from marinades
items.content: If the meat was marinated before grilling, it may contain added salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grilled chicken legs, drumsticks and thighs can be served as a main dish, sliced for salads, added to soups, or used in sandwiches. The skin can be eaten with the meat or removed after cooking if a lower‑calorie option is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it keeps quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.
